Record the scope boundary, ownership roles and the authorization contract.

Bind the per-URL acquisition guard to the ownership transition.
Give the failed state terminal or backoff-gated semantics.
Keep workers alive until a scan-level stop condition, or respawn them on new work.

Deduplicate discovery records or store corroboration as provenance.
Consult the content fingerprint index or remove it.

Drive the worker pool from the adaptive counter, or delete the feature.
Introduce an acquisition-provider boundary.
Define and persist a scan-level termination evaluator.

Canonical machine-readable analysis record (docs/analysis/analysis.json, governed by docs/analysis/analysis.schema.json) with tools/validate-analysis.mjs and tools/render-claims.mjs. Classified DOC_CLEANUP because the primary artifact is the record; the validator and renderer are its enforcement. Reason: a canonical state model that cannot be machine-validated silently drifts out of step with the documents
regenerate every status statement in the five typed fields Reason: claim records, evidence register and behaviour documents must use one vocabulary or the checks cannot detect substitution

Claim-level semantic validation (C-001…C-043 plus cross-dimension rules; renumbered to the canonical CV matrix by R-019), canonical authorization fields with explicit operation sets and intersection semantics, no-inheritance enforcement, and a YAML mirror of the authorization object checked by serialization invariants SER-001…SER-012. Reason: structure alone does not make a claim semantically valid, and a level name must not imply an operation

Replace the level-as-operation-set authorization with level profiles, capability sets and operation resolution; split execution and post-verification into separate lifecycles with per-operation results; add the confidence dimension and the validation matrix CV-001…CV-020. Reason: a profile name must not imply a capability, and an execution result must not imply a verification result

Separate the two verification domains (claim verification versus execution verification), make capabilities first-class objects with lifecycle states and resource classes, add per-operation authorization decisions, and adopt the normative AC-001…AC-016 and EVV-001…EVV-009 rule sets (the authorization half was replaced by CAP-001…CAP-016/CG-001…CG-015 and the section 216 function in R-021). Reason: an unqualified "verification" field does not say what is being verified, and DECLARED is not ENABLED

Adopt the machine-validatable closed schema of brief 10 (sections 209-211, additionalProperties: false), move policy data out of the record into an external capability registry, replace the capabilities{grants,denies} object with explicit capability grant objects carrying capability_id and state, and renumber the claim identifiers into the CLAIM-nnn namespace. Reason: a record that cannot be validated by a closed schema cannot be audited mechanically, and a capability grant that is not an explicit object cannot be told apart from a profile declaration.
